name: Hagia Sophia
description: Built as a cathedral in 537, it became a mosque in 1453, a museum in 1934 and a mosque again in 2020. Its huge dome still dominates the old city.

name: Topkapı Palace
description: The Ottoman sultans’ palace for nearly 400 years: a series of courtyards, the harem, the treasury and views over the Bosphorus.

name: Hippodrome
description: The long square on the site of the ancient chariot-racing track, with an Egyptian obelisk and other monuments along its middle.

name: Süleymaniye Mosque
description: The great 16th-century mosque on a hill above the Golden Horn, with a vast domed prayer hall, gardens and a cemetery.

name: Çemberlitaş Hamam
description: A Turkish bath built in 1584 and still in use, with separate domed marble halls for men and women.

name: Galata Bridge
description: The bridge across the Golden Horn, with a tram and road on top, fishermen along the rails, and fish restaurants on the lower level.

name: Rumeli Fortress
description: A fortress built by the Ottomans in 1452 on the European shore of the Bosphorus, a year before they took Constantinople.

name: Galata Tower
description: A round stone tower built by the Genoese in 1348, with a viewing balcony over the Golden Horn and the old city.

name: Galata Mevlevi Lodge
description: A former lodge of the Mevlevi order, the whirling dervishes, now a museum with the wooden hall where their ceremony took place.

name: Theodosian Walls
description: A stretch of the 5th-century walls that guarded Constantinople’s land side, at the gate named after the Ottoman cannon of the 1453 siege.

name: Grand Bazaar
description: One of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world: thousands of shops in a maze of vaulted lanes.
